key_insight: OrbitTAMP grounds language-model intent into a hierarchical task-and-motion planning pipeline, turning partial natural-language spacecraft rendezvous commands into physically valid mission plans and trajectories.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce the expertise bottleneck in spacecraft rendezvous and proximity operations by making planning more scalable, auditable, and easier to interface with through natural language.
method: LLM converts a command into a partial mission specification.
Domain planners fill in missing decisions using a graph of reusable behaviors and admissible maneuvers.
Trajectory optimization produces a dynamically feasible spacecraft trajectory.
evidence_signal: In numerical tests, the system achieved 98% exact recovery of partial mission specifications with frontier LLMs, and verifier-guided revision boosted a 9B model from 75% to 88%.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the behavior graph, planner modules, and verifier, so errors or missing constraints in the domain model could still produce invalid or suboptimal plans.
paper_title: OrbitTAMP: Grounding Language Models for Task and Motion Planning in Spacecraft Rendezvous
